name: Challenge Manufacturing
old_description: Founded in Walker, MI with a single mission and machine, Challenge Manufacturing has seen remarkable growth in its 40-year journey. With over 3,000 employees and a presence in 12 strategic locations nationwide, we proudly supply automotive components to our valued customers. Despite rapid expansion, our commitment to our team and customers remains our core focus.
about:
Challenge Manufacturing began in 1981 in Walker, Michigan, with a single press machine and a mission to supply automotive components. The company is employee-owned through an ESOP structure, a distinction it says cultivates collective dedication and accountability.

Today the firm operates across 12 U.S. locations with more than 3,000 employee-owners. Its core processes include stamping, welding, and assembly, supported by over 1,500 industrial robots. The company traces its growth from a single press operation to a comprehensive manufacturing footprint. As a Tier 1 supplier, it produces components for the world's largest automotive manufacturers.

The customer base is concentrated in the automotive sector, where Challenge serves major OEMs as a contract manufacturer of structural and assembled parts. No other industries are cited in the company's public materials.

Leadership emphasizes an Operating System built on six pillars—safety, quality, delivery, cost, people, and maintenance—to drive operational excellence. The ESOP model is presented as the foundation for continuous improvement and long-term customer satisfaction. Employee engagement programs and community volunteering are also highlighted as cultural differentiators.

name: Champion Foods, Inc
old_description: Champion Foods is a domestic and international food distribution company that services clients throughout a variety of industries, large and small.  Founded in 1985, Champion Foods is a family-owned company based in Baton Rouge, LA, with offices in San Francisco, Atlanta, Chicago, Wisconsin, and New York. Despite our growth, we are still able to offer personalized services to our clients, which we believe are unrivaled in the industry.
about:
Champion Foods, Inc. was founded in 1985 as a family-owned business in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. The company began as a food distribution operation serving the Gulf South region and has since expanded to maintain offices in San Francisco, Atlanta, Chicago, Wisconsin, and New York.

The firm operates as a domestic and international food distributor, handling a wide portfolio that includes Mexican sugar for the U.S. market and Brazilian sugar (ICUMSA 45, 150, and 600‑1200) for export worldwide. Its product lines cover frozen vegetables, sweet‑potato and white‑potato items, breakfast products, avocado pulp and flavored guacamole, edamame, breaded vegetables and appetizers, and assorted canned goods. Champion Foods leverages distribution technology and scheduled delivery services to manage inventory and reduce out‑of‑stock situations for its customers.

Its customer base spans food‑service distributors, industrial manufacturers, retail grocery chains, offshore catering companies, ship chandlers, cruise lines, and the marine and petroleum industries of the Gulf of Mexico. The company also identifies itself as a kosher and international food distributor.

Champion Foods emphasizes personalized service that it describes as unrivaled in the industry, along with proprietary software that monitors profitable items and advises on inventory planning. The business was built to provide a cost‑effective solution that saves clients time and money while maintaining product quality and shelf life.

about:
Champion Solar was founded in 2010 in Minnesota City, Minnesota, and has since served homeowners and businesses across Minnesota and western Wisconsin. The company operates with local, in-house crews rather than subcontractors, emphasizing a family-values culture guided by honesty, respect, trust, integrity, loyalty, and empathy.

The firm delivers turnkey solar photovoltaic systems, including custom design, permitting, utility paperwork, installation, net metering enrollment, and ongoing monitoring and warranty support. It also installs electric-vehicle chargers, handles insurance claims for solar assets, and coordinates roof replacements when needed. All panels installed are sourced from U.S. manufacturers.

Customers range from residential homeowners to commercial facilities and educational institutions such as Deep Portage Learning Center, which received an 18 kW system. The company's service territory covers the Rochester, Rogers, and Winona areas, among others.

Champion Solar differentiates itself through a workmanship warranty, a commitment to American-made panels for quality and supply-chain security, and an annual tree-planting partnership with the Mississippi Valley Conservancy. Its stated mission is to put money back in customers' pockets while reducing carbon emissions for future generations.

name: Champion Used Auto Parts
old_description: In business since 1992, our staff at Champion Used Auto Parts are specialists when it comes to all kinds of automobile parts. Motors, transmissions, alternators, rotors, headlights – we have everything that you might need. We also offer deliveries in the tri-state area. Our used auto parts all include a 101-day warranty.
about:
Champion Used Auto Parts has operated from Valley Lee, Maryland, since 1992. The company specializes in supplying recycled automotive components to customers across the tri-state region. No founders are named in public records, and ownership structure has not been disclosed.

The business maintains a computerized inventory of used parts for virtually any make and model, covering American and foreign vehicles. Stock includes engines, transmissions, alternators, rotors, headlights, and other components, all tested before sale. A 101-day warranty backs every part. The facility also operates a certified scale for purchasing scrap metal and whole vehicles by weight. Delivery service extends within a 150-mile radius of Valley Lee.

Customers range from individual vehicle owners and rideshare drivers to repair shops seeking cost-effective replacements for trucks, sports cars, and daily drivers. The company positions its offerings as a fraction of new-part pricing without sacrificing reliability.

The operation emphasizes that it does not carry low-quality imitation parts, instead focusing on tested, reliable used components. The 101-day warranty and computerized lookup system are cited as key differentiators in a market where buyers often face uncertainty about part condition.

about:
Champion Wire & Cable, LLC was founded in 1995 in Freehold, New Jersey. The company operates as a distributor of wire and cable products, with its corporate headquarters in Westbury, New York, and additional distribution centers in Freehold, NJ; Tempe, AZ; and Houston, TX.

The company supplies wire and cable for utility, industrial, commercial, and transportation markets. Its value-added services include cut-to-length cutting, custom paralleling, custom printing, custom striping, and custom cable design developed with manufacturing partners. Champion maintains a multi-million-dollar inventory across its national distribution network and offers same-day shipping on stocked items.

Champion serves a broad range of industries: electric power generation, transmission, and distribution; battery energy storage systems; renewables including solar photovoltaic, wind, geothermal, and hydropower; high-temperature low-sag conductors; factory automation, manufacturing, water treatment, oil and gas, mining, marine, petrochemical, EPC, aerospace, and agriculture; data centers, building wire, fire alarm, security, HVAC, fiber optics; and transportation sectors such as EV charging, rail, mass transit, overhead catenary systems, and airport lighting. Its customers include distributors, contractors, and engineering firms.

The company emphasizes its "Champion Advantage": strategically located distribution centers to reduce lead times, a suite of value-added services that save installation time, and an experienced sales team that provides technical guidance and responsive service.

name: Checker Bag Co.
old_description: Quality packaging enhances your product. We know how critical your identity is with customers, which is why we’ve been in business since 1875. With different sizes, thicknesses, and shapes—including flat, gusseted, and ziplock—our bags meet your every need. They are lightweight, flexible, cost-effective, recyclable, and reusable, making them excellent for e-commerce, retail, and industrial applications.
about:
Checker Bag Co. has operated from St. Louis, Missouri, since its founding in 1875.

The company produces custom plastic bags in three primary material families: cellophane, polypropylene, and polyethylene. Its capabilities include custom printing, and the fabrication of bags with features such as metal grommets, zip-lock closures, wickets, headers, tamper-evident seals, die-cut shapes, and micro-perforations. Bag styles range from flat and gusseted to ziplock configurations, serving applications from food packaging to industrial uses.

Checker Bag serves customers across advertising, bakeries, distribution, food processing, industrial, produce, retail, chemical, and wholesale sectors. Its client base spans small local shops to large industrial bakeries, with documented work for ice companies, sourdough bakeries, and candy producers.

The company highlights its SAI Global Good Manufacturing Practices certification for polypropylene bag production as a key differentiator, alongside a stated emphasis on customer service and the ability to provide film and printed prototypes during development.

Chicago Fabrications was founded in 2012 in Chicago, Illinois. The company began as a design and build firm focused on refined wood joinery, metal welding, and structural fabrication.

Its capabilities span brand activations, trade show exhibits, retail displays, pop-up builds, custom furniture and fixtures, event builds, interior renovations, scenic elements, and specialty fabrication. Work is executed in-house, combining wood joinery, metal welding, and structural fabrication, with design, production, logistics, and installation managed under one roof.

name: Chicago Metal Fabricators
old_description: From concept to completion, Chicago Metal Fabricators is committed to exceeding customer expectations and creating quality custom component solutions that meet precise specifications, quality standards, and on-time delivery deadlines.
about:
Founded in 1908 on Chicago's South Side, Chicago Metal Fabricators operates as part of the Nalbach Group, a conglomerate of companies specializing in custom automation machinery and fabricated components. The company began as a metal cabinet and ductwork fabricator before expanding into heavy and light gauge metal fabrication across three integrated facilities.

The company provides comprehensive metal fabrication services including welding (FCAW, GMAW, GTAW, SAW, robotic, and laser), press brake forming up to 1,500 tons and 32-foot width, flat laser cutting with large-format fiber lasers, and high-definition plasma cutting on a 70-foot Messer table. Operations span over 300,000 square feet across two heavy-metal plants in Chicago (250,000 sq ft) and a 60,000 sq ft light-gauge facility in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, supporting prototype through high-volume production and full assembly.

Chicago Metal Fabricators serves rail, aerospace, defense, air ground support, construction, energy storage, infrastructure, off-highway/utility, water treatment, point-of-purchase, and art installation markets. Documented projects include rail locomotive rear wall and restroom assemblies, particle accelerator base weldments and concrete forms, and a 100-ton forklift mast weldment fabricated from 3-inch A514 T-1 and A572-Gr 80 plate.

The company emphasizes its "one stop shop" model, integrating reverse engineering, prototyping, mass production, and assembly under ISO 9001:2015, AWS, and ITAR certifications. It cites its ability to adapt with innovative design concepts and advancing technology, along with efficient technology and skilled expertise to ensure accuracy, durability, and cost savings, as the foundation for its century-long success.
